goal_summary: Build a modular, responsive, fully functional React calculator application with history tracking, keyboard support, and clean separation of concerns via a pure calculator engine.

phases.name: Foundation & Engine
phases.description: Implement the pure calculation engine and reusable display/button components. This phase establishes the core logic and visual primitives before building the full calculator.
deliverables: calculatorEngine.js — pure arithmetic state machine with +, -, *, /, %, decimal, clear, backspace operations
Button.jsx — reusable styled button component with variant support (number, operator, function, equals)
Display.jsx — read-only display showing current expression and result with overflow handling

phases.name: Core Calculator Assembly
phases.description: Assemble the main calculator components: Keypad grid, HistoryLog, and the Calculator orchestrator that wires everything together with state management and keyboard event handling.
deliverables: Keypad.jsx — grid layout for all calculator buttons with dynamic configuration
HistoryLog.jsx — scrollable history log with click-to-restore and clear functionality
Calculator.jsx — main orchestrator managing state, engine integration, keyboard shortcuts, and localStorage persistence

phases.name: Styling & Entry Points
phases.description: Create the CSS stylesheet with modern dark theme, responsive grid, and accessibility features. Set up the React entry points (App.jsx, index.jsx) to mount the calculator.
deliverables: calculator.css — dark theme with CSS custom properties, responsive grid, hover/active states, reduced motion support
App.jsx — root component wrapping Calculator with theme provider
index.jsx — React mount point with strict mode

phases.name: Testing & Quality Assurance
phases.description: Write automated tests for the calculator engine logic, component interactions, and keyboard event simulation. Conduct a quality audit for responsiveness, edge cases, and adherence to design constraints.
deliverables: Unit tests for calculatorEngine.js — all operations, edge cases, error handling
Integration tests for Calculator component — button clicks, keyboard events, history interactions
Quality audit report — responsiveness verification, modularity check, edge-case handling

milestones: Engine foundation complete: calculatorEngine.js handles all operations correctly
Core UI assembled: Calculator renders with full keypad, display, and history log
Application fully functional: All operations work via clicks and keyboard shortcuts
Quality gate passed: All tests pass, responsive on all devices, edge cases handled

risk_mitigations.risk: Division by zero produces NaN or Infinity
risk_mitigations.mitigation: Engine catches division by zero and returns 'Error' string; display shows error state until cleared

risk_mitigations.risk: Keyboard event conflicts with browser shortcuts
risk_mitigations.mitigation: Use keydown listener with preventDefault for calculator keys; map only specific keys (0-9, operators, Enter, Escape, Backspace)

risk_mitigations.risk: State desync between engine and UI
risk_mitigations.mitigation: Single source of truth in Calculator.jsx; engine functions are pure (no side effects); all state changes flow through one handler

risk_mitigations.risk: Responsive layout breaks on small screens
risk_mitigations.mitigation: CSS Grid with minmax() for button sizing; media queries for viewport-specific adjustments; touch-friendly button sizes (min 44px)
Limit history to 50 entries with auto-trim; store only essential data (expression, result, timestamp)

success_criteria: All basic operations (+, -, *, /) produce correct results
Percentage operation works correctly (x% → x/100, ±% → negate percentage)
Clear (C) and All-Clear (AC) functions work as expected
Backspace deletes last character or last operand
Decimal point handling prevents multiple decimals per number
Keyboard shortcuts: numbers, operators, Enter (=), Escape (AC), Backspace
History log records all calculations and allows click-to-restore
Application is responsive: usable on mobile, tablet, and desktop
Code is modular: each component has a single responsibility and is independently testable
Calculator engine is pure: no React dependencies, easily unit-testable
